issues.description: The problem requires printing each book's title from Client (Client.main prints '<book.title> by <book.author>'), implying Book.title must be accessible. In the solution, Book.title is declared as 'private let title', which makes it inaccessible outside the Book struct and thus prevents Client (in a different file) from accessing book.title. This is a visibility mismatch that would cause compilation errors or block students from implementing the intended behavior.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Book.title property at least internal (module-visible) so Client can access it. For example, change 'private let title: String' to 'let title: String' (or 'public let title: String' if broader visibility is desired) in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift. Ensure access levels for the other properties match intended usage.
